A ladder 14 m long leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground. Find the height reached by the ladder on the wall and the distance of its foot from the wall. (Use $\sqrt3=1.73$)
questions.answer: Height $=14\sin60^\circ=14\times\frac{\sqrt3}2=7\sqrt3=7\times1.73=12.11$ m. Distance of foot from wall $=14\cos60^\circ=14\times\frac12=7$ m.

questions.text: From a window 20 m above the ground in a street, the angle of elevation of the top of the opposite house is $60^\circ$ and the angle of depression of its foot is $30^\circ$. Find the height of the opposite house.
questions.answer: Let the horizontal distance between window and house be $d$. Foot: $\tan30^\circ=\frac{20}{d}\Rightarrow d=20\sqrt3$ m. Top above window level: $d\tan60^\circ=20\sqrt3\times\sqrt3=60$ m. Height of the house $=20+60=80$ m.

questions.text: A boy 1.5 m tall stands 30 m from a building. The angle of elevation of the top of the building from his eyes is $30^\circ$. Find the height of the building. (Use $\sqrt3=1.73$)
questions.answer: Height of building above the boy's eye level $=30\tan30^\circ=\frac{30}{\sqrt3}=10\sqrt3=17.3$ m. Total height $=17.3+1.5=18.8$ m.

questions.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from a point A on the ground is $45^\circ$. On moving 30 m towards the building to a point B, the angle of elevation of the top becomes $60^\circ$. Find the height of the building and the distance of B from its foot. (Use $\sqrt3=1.73$)
questions.answer: Let the height be $h$ and the foot be $P$. At A: $\tan45^\circ=\frac{h}{AP}\Rightarrow AP=h$. At B: $\tan60^\circ=\frac{h}{BP}\Rightarrow BP=\frac h{\sqrt3}$. $AP-BP=30\Rightarrow h\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)=30\Rightarrow h=\frac{30\sqrt3}{\sqrt3-1}=\frac{30\sqrt3(\sqrt3+1)}2=15(3+\sqrt3)=15\times4.73=70.95$ m. $BP=\frac h{\sqrt3}=15(\sqrt3+1)=15\times2.73=40.95$ m. Height $\approx70.95$ m; B is $\approx40.95$ m from the foot.

questions.text: From the top of a 60 m high building, the angles of depression of the top and the bottom of a tower are $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ respectively. Find the height of the tower and the horizontal distance between the building and the tower. (Use $\sqrt3=1.73$)
questions.answer: Let the horizontal distance be $d$. Bottom of tower: $\tan60^\circ=\frac{60}{d}\Rightarrow d=\frac{60}{\sqrt3}=20\sqrt3=34.6$ m. The top of the tower is below the building top by $d\tan30^\circ=20\sqrt3\times\frac1{\sqrt3}=20$ m. Height of tower $=60-20=40$ m.

questions.text: Two poles of equal height stand on either side of a road 80 m wide. At a point on the road between the poles, the angles of elevation of the tops of the poles are $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$. Find the height of the poles and the distances of the point from the poles. (Use $\sqrt3=1.73$)
questions.answer: Let the point be $P$, at distance $x$ from the pole with elevation $60^\circ$ and $80-x$ from the other. $h=x\tan60^\circ=x\sqrt3$ and $h=(80-x)\tan30^\circ=\frac{80-x}{\sqrt3}$. So $3x=80-x\Rightarrow x=20$. $h=20\sqrt3=34.6$ m. The point is 20 m from one pole and 60 m from the other; each pole is 34.6 m high.

questions.text: Find a quadratic polynomial whose sum and product of zeroes are $-3$ and $2$ respectively.
If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the zeroes of $x^2-7x+10$, find the value of $\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta$.
For what value of $k$ does the pair of equations $2x+3y=7$ and $(k-1)x+(k+2)y=3k$ have infinitely many solutions?
questions.answer: $\frac2{k-1}=\frac3{k+2}=\frac7{3k}$. From the first two: $2k+4=3k-3\Rightarrow k=7$. Check: $\frac26=\frac39=\frac7{21}=\frac13$. So $k=7$.

The following distribution is given:
| Class | 0 - 20 | 20 - 40 | 40 - 60 | 60 - 80 | 80 - 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 10 | 9 | 12 | 6 |
Write the modal class and the median class.
questions.answer: Highest frequency 12, so the modal class is 60 - 80. $N=40$, $\frac N2=20$; cumulative frequencies 3, 13, 22, 34, 40; 20 lies in the third class, so the median class is 40 - 60.

questions.text: The mean of 5 numbers is 18. If one number is excluded, the mean of the remaining numbers is 16. Find the excluded number.
questions.answer: Sum of 5 numbers $=90$; sum of remaining 4 $=64$. Excluded number $=90-64=26$.

questions.text: Find the distance between the points $(a, b)$ and $(-a, -b)$.
Find the ratio in which the $y$-axis divides the line segment joining $(-4,-6)$ and $(10,12)$.
questions.answer: Let the ratio be $k:1$. On the $y$-axis $x=0$: $\frac{10k-4}{k+1}=0\Rightarrow k=\frac25$. The ratio is $2:5$ (internally).

questions.text: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. Find the probability of getting at most one head.
questions.answer: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. At most one head: HT, TH, TT, so $P=\frac34$.

If one zero of the polynomial $p(x)=x^2-5x+k$ is 2, find the value of $k$ and the other zero.
questions.answer: $p(2)=0\Rightarrow4-10+k=0\Rightarrow k=6$. Sum of zeroes $=5$, so the other zero $=5-2=3$.

questions.text: A school librarian has 120 English books, 144 Hindi books and 168 Maths books. She wants to arrange them in stacks so that every stack has the same number of books of each language and no book is left over, and the number of stacks is as large as possible.

subparts.text: Express 144 as a product of prime factors.
Find the HCF of 120, 144 and 168.
What is the greatest number of stacks that can be made?
subparts.answer: The number of stacks must divide each count, so it is the HCF: 24 stacks.

subparts.text: How many books are there in each stack?
subparts.answer: English $120\div24=5$, Hindi $144\div24=6$, Maths $168\div24=7$; $5+6+7=18$ books in each stack.

questions.text: The length of a rectangular garden is 5 m more than its breadth. The area of the garden is 150 m$^2$. Let the breadth of the garden be $x$ metres.

subparts.text: Form the quadratic equation in $x$ that represents the given situation.
Solve the equation to find the breadth and the length of the garden.
subparts.answer: $x^2+15x-10x-150=0\Rightarrow(x+15)(x-10)=0\Rightarrow x=10$ (breadth cannot be negative). Breadth $=10$ m, length $=15$ m.

questions.text: Twenty cards numbered 1 to 20 are placed in a box and mixed well. One card is drawn at random.

subparts.text: Find the probability that the number on the card is a multiple of 5.
Find the probability that the number on the card is a prime number.
Find the probability that the number on the card is greater than 15.
Find the probability that the number on the card is neither prime nor composite.
subparts.answer: Only 1 is neither prime nor composite; $P=\frac1{20}$.

questions.text: A circular park has centre $O$ and radius 6 m. A gate $P$ is located 10 m from the centre $O$. Two straight paths $PA$ and $PB$ from the gate touch the boundary of the park at points $A$ and $B$ respectively.

subparts.text: What is the measure of $\angle OAP$? Give a reason.
subparts.answer: $90^\circ$, because the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

subparts.text: Find the length of the path $PA$.
Find the length of $PB$ and the area of the quadrilateral $OAPB$.
subparts.answer: $PB=PA=8$ m (tangents from an external point). $OAPB$ consists of two right triangles $OAP$ and $OBP$: area $=2\times\frac12\times6\times8=48\ \mathrm{m^2}$.
